turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was dead set against it, he said, and he would not have O-lan leave him and their son behind.
turns.speech: O-lan, you speak of death as if it were a thing to be welcomed, but I will not have it! I will not have you leave me and our son behind.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would not leave their son, and that she would stay with him until he was married and settled.
turns.speech: I will not leave my son, I will stay with him until he is married and settled.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's voice trembled with emotion as he spoke, his words spilling out in a rush. How could she think such thoughts? O-lan was his wife, his companion, his friend. She would not leave him, not now, not ever.
turns.speech: O-lan, how can you think such thoughts? You are my wife, my companion, my friend. You will not leave me, not now, not ever.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was old now, and she had not long to live. She wanted to see their son married and settled before she went.
turns.speech: I am old now, Wang Lung, and I have not long to live. I want to see our son married and settled before I go.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son spoke reassuringly, his voice calm and steady, as he said, Mother, don't worry, he'll take care of everything, he promised. He'll marry soon and be settled, just like she wants.
turns.speech: Mother, don't worry, I'll take care of everything, I promise. I'll marry soon and be settled, just like you want.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung would not let O-lan go, she would stay with him, and he would take care of her until the end.
turns.speech: I will not let you go, O-lan. You will stay with me, and I will take care of you until the end.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was too old now, she thought, it was time for her to think of their son's future, not of her own.
turns.speech: I am too old now, Wang Lung. It is time for me to think of our son's future, not of my own.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was torn with anguish, he thought of leaving him, and he wondered what he would do without O-lan. What will he do without her? She was his life, his everything, and the thought of living without her was unbearable.
turns.speech: Why must you think of leaving me? You are my life, O-lan. What will I do without you?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was tired, she had thought of this, and she knew what she wanted. She wanted their son to be happy, and she wanted him to be settled before she went.
turns.speech: I am tired, Wang Lung. I have thought of this, and I know what I want. I want our son to be happy, and I want him to be settled before I go.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He told O-lan, Don't worry, Mother, he'll take care of everything, just like she's always taking care of him.
turns.speech: Don't worry, Mother, I'll take care of everything, just like you're always taking care of me.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was dead set against O-lan leaving him, not yet, not until he had made sure that their son was settled and happy. O-lan was his life, and he would not let her go.
turns.speech: O-lan, you must not think of leaving me, not yet, not until I have made sure that our son is settled and happy. You are my life, and I will not let you go.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan knew what her eldest son wanted, but what would happen to him after she was gone? Who would take care of him then?
turns.speech: I know what you want, son, but what will happen to you after I'm gone? Who will take care of you then?

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He told O-lan, he would take care of himself, don't worry about him. Father would be here to help him, and he would make sure to work hard and make them both proud.
turns.speech: Mother, I'll take care of myself, don't worry about me. Father will be here to help me, and I'll make sure to work hard and make you both proud.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's eyes clouded with worry as she asked, What about when Father is not here, who will take care of him then?
turns.speech: What about when Father is not here? Who will take care of him then?

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung spoke sharply, his voice low and urgent. Don't speak like this, O-lan. He would be here to take care of their son, to make sure he was safe and happy. He would not leave him to fend for himself.
turns.speech: Don't speak like this, O-lan. I will be here to take care of our son, to make sure he is safe and happy. I will not leave him to fend for himself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan knew Father wanted to take care of Wang Lung, but what would happen when she was gone and the house was empty?
turns.speech: I know Father wants to take care of him, but what will happen when I am gone and the house is empty?

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He was fine, he told O-lan, he would take care of himself and make Wang Lung and her proud. He would work hard and bring home food for the family.
turns.speech: Don't worry, Mother, I'll be fine. I'll take care of myself and make you and Father proud. I'll work hard and bring home food for the family.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung spoke softly, his voice a gentle breeze on a summer's day, as he said, O-lan, don't talk like this. He would be here to take care of her, to make sure she was comfortable and at peace. She must not worry about him, or the son, or the household.
turns.speech: O-lan, don't talk like this. I will be here to take care of you, to make sure you are comfortable and at peace. You must not worry about me, or the son, or the household.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: But what of the debt to the landlord, Wang Lung? Who will pay it when O-lan is gone?
turns.speech: But what of the debt to the landlord, Wang Lung? Who will pay it when I am gone?

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son spoke reassuringly, his voice steady, as he said, Don't worry, Mother, he would take care of the debt to the landlord, he would work hard and bring in a good harvest, they would be fine.
turns.speech: Don't worry, Mother, I'll take care of the debt to the landlord, I'll work hard and bring in a good harvest, we'll be fine.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
